notes: A.1 item 146 (cite.py --check A.1 'RECORD clause (calculations to derive size of records on storage medium)' -> OK §A.1 146): required + documented. §13.18.43.4 GR2 'The implementor shall specify the calculations necessary for the user to derive the size for records on the storage medium' (cite.py --check 13.18.43.4 -> OK 2)). docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has NO DOC-A.1-146 row (audit_annex_a1.py does not list 146). The only related text is DOC-A.1-151 (4-byte LE length prefix for variable-length record sequential/relative/indexed; line delimiters for LINE SEQUENTIAL), which answers GR5 of §12.4.5.11 for VARIABLE records only and states no calculation for fixed-length files, nor for CODE-SET's effect (GR2 names CODE-SET and FORMAT as factors). Probe probe/rec/p1.cob: fixed FD F1 (01 X(5)) writes two unframed 5-byte records (10-byte file); implicit Format 1 F4 (X(5)+X(10)) pads every record to 10 bytes unframed; Format 3 F3 writes 4-byte-prefixed frames (0x05000000 'ABCDE' ...). So the calculation is fixed in code (fixed: record size; variable: 4 + record size) but not documented. Harm silent. Owning note kb/Work PB1278 (open, claims item 146) — cited, not re-reported.

A.1 item 147 (cite.py --check A.1 'RECORD clause (implicit RECORD clause if RECORD clause is not specified)' -> OK §A.1 147): required + documented. §13.18.43.4 GR5 'This implicit RECORD clause is defined by the implementor' (cite.py --check 13.18.43.4 -> OK 5)). docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has NO DOC-A.1-147 row. A determination exists only in prose outside the register: §3 D-FRA (iv) ('the implicit RECORD clause ... is Format 2 when a record is variable-length ... and Format 1 otherwise'), which audit_annex_a1.py does not count and no inventory anchor resolves to. Code: FileModel.ImpliesVariableFormat = Varying is null && RecordContains is null && any variable-length record; else implied Format 1 at the largest record. Probe probe/rec/p1.cob F4 (01 X(5), 01 X(10), no RECORD clause): both records written as 10 bytes, consistent with GR5 a). Edges NOT conforming per kb/Work PB1276 (row GR-13.18.43.4-5 PARTIAL: implied Format 2 minimum inherits the GR8 national byte-count defect) and PB322 determination F (a RECORD-clause-less SD releases at record-name-1's own size) — cited, not re-reported. Harm silent (the missing §7 row). No kb/Work note claims DOC-A.1-147 (PB1278 claims 146/148 only; PB1276 mentions item 147 but its inventory_rows do not include it) — NEW finding, clustered with PB1278.

A.1 item 148 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 148): required + documented. §13.18.43.4 GR17 'It is implementor defined whether format 3 of the RECORD clause produces fixed-length records or variable-length records' (cite.py --check 13.18.43.4 -> OK 17)). docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has NO DOC-A.1-148 row, and no prose elsewhere states the choice. Code answers VARIABLE: probe probe/rec/p1.cob FD F3 RECORD CONTAINS 5 TO 10 CHARACTERS writes a 5-byte and a 10-byte record as two 4-byte-length-prefixed frames (0x05 00 00 00 'ABCDE' 0x0A 00 00 00 'ABCDEFGHIJ'), i.e. variable-length. Behaviour is fixed but undocumented => DIVERGES, harm silent. Same framing re-probed at --std 85 (identical bytes). Owning note kb/Work PB1278 (open, claims item 148) — cited, not re-reported.

A.1 item 149 (cite.py --check A.1 'RECORD DELIMITER clause (consistency rules when used with external file connectors)' -> OK §A.1 149): CONDITIONALLY required, 'conditioned upon the existence of the optional feature-name in the RECORD DELIMITER clause'. The rule it points at is §12.4.5.3 GR1 c) (A.1 writes '12.4.5, General rule 1c'): 'The implementor shall specify the consistency rules for feature-name-1' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.3 -> OK 1) c)). A.1 preamble: 'Conditionally required: If the associated feature or language element is implemented then this element is also required.' (verbatim in §A.1 preamble). The feature is NOT implemented: docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-150 records feature-name-1 as 'Not provided.' (empty set; a written feature-name is accepted-inert with COBOLNET1778, §2 row 26 declines the whole RECORD DELIMITER clause). So the obligation cannot be incurred — but §7 has NO DOC-A.1-149 row saying so, and no derived-verdicts selector covers a CONDITIONALLY-required item whose condition is absent (a1-optional-not-provided selects requirement=optional only; evaluated with scripts/spec/inventory_schema.DerivedSelector over this row: not selected). Whether such a row closes as DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT (by a §7 'Not provided — condition absent' row, or by extending PB280 Q1's selector to the conditionally-required class) is an owner decision, not an adjudicator's. Owning register: kb/Work A11 (open). No per-item note found (grep 'item 149' / 'DOC-A.1-149' over kb/Work: none).

A.1 item 152 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 152): CONDITIONALLY required, 'conditioned on the existence of such circumstances in an implementation'; documented if provided. §9.1.16: 'The implementor may specify circumstances other than a locked logical record that result in the return of a locked record status.' (cite.py --check 9.1.16 -> OK). Code read: status 51 (FileStatusCode.RecordLocked) is produced at exactly two sites — PhysicalFileTable.LockRecord (the record id is held by ANOTHER connector) and FileRegistry.ConflictOnLockedRecord (IsLockedByOther on the target record id); the FileRegistry.cs:1635 use only compares it for RETRY FOREVER. Locks are per logical record id (no block / index-reorganization locking), so no other circumstance returns 51: the implementation provides NO such circumstances and the condition is absent. docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has no DOC-A.1-152 row stating that, and no derived-verdicts selector covers a CONDITIONALLY-required A.1 item whose condition is absent (a1-optional-not-provided is requirement=optional only; DerivedSelector evaluated over this row: not selected). Whether this closes as DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT / CONFORMS on a 'None.' §7 row, or via a class selector, is an owner decision (same question as DOC-A.1-149). Editions: record locking exists from 2002 (Annex E), not probed per edition. Owning register kb/Work A11; no per-item note (grep 'item 152'/'DOC-A.1-152' over kb/Work: none).

A.1 item 154 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 154): required, at least 255, documented. §12.4.5.9.4 GR7 (A.1 writes '12.4.5.9, LOCK MODE clause, General rule 7'): 'The implementor shall specify the maximum number of record locks that may be held by a run unit; that maximum shall be at least 255' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.4 -> OK 7)). Code: PhysicalFileTable.RunUnitLockMax = 255; LockRecord and PreflightNewLock return 53 (RunUnitLockLimit) when TotalRunUnitLocks() >= 255 (the table is one instance per FileRegistry, i.e. per run unit). The value meets the >= 255 floor and the 'unsuccessful ... I-O status that indicates that condition' half returns 53. Pinned by unit:CobolFileLockTests.RunUnitLockLimit_256thRunUnitLock_Is53. BUT docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has NO DOC-A.1-154 row, and grep of CONFORMANCE.md for '255'/'53'/lock ceiling finds no statement of the run-unit maximum anywhere => the required documentation is absent: DIVERGES, harm silent. No kb/Work note claims item 154 (PB707 is about the RETRY path of 53/54, inventory_rows []; PB671 is citation labels) — NEW finding.

A.1 item 155 (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 155): required, at least 15, documented. §12.4.5.9.4 GR7: 'The implementor shall specify the maximum number of record locks that may be held by a file connector; that maximum shall be at least 15' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.4 -> OK 7)). Code: PhysicalFileTable.ConnectorLockMax = 15; LockRecord / PreflightNewLock count the locks the connector name holds on the physical file and return 54 (ConnectorLockLimit) at the 16th. Meets the >= 15 floor; pinned by unit:CobolFileLockTests.ConnectorLockLimit_16thRecord_Is54. docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 has NO DOC-A.1-155 row and no statement of the per-connector maximum anywhere => DIVERGES, harm silent. No kb/Work note claims item 155 — NEW finding (same mechanism as DOC-A.1-154).
